newsitem.title: CANADA: Imax Corp shares rise on Q4 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Imax Corp shares rise on Q4 earnings.

text.p: Imax Corp shares rose C$0.25 a share to C$43 on the Toronto Stock Exchange after the 3-Dimensional film company reported fourth quarter earnings quadrupled in 1996.

Co-chief executive Richard Gelfond said he feels Imax has barely scratched the surface in terms of growth for its theater technology after setting a blistering pace in 1996 which saw Imax sign contracts for eight IMAX theatre systems worth C$27.3 million in the fourth quarter alone.
"When you look at a world map you see a tremendous underpenetration and we've been aggressively exploiting that."

Gelfond said the company is reaping the benefits of a process begun in 1994, when he and his partner decided to move Imax into mainstream entertainment from a mainly science- oriented presentation. He also said Imax was riding the wave of aggressive expansion by theater chain owners.
"As part of our migration into mainstream commercial entertainment we've been doing a lot more business with the cinema chains."
Gelfond said Imax will continue to exploit its advances in commercial film and is working on technology for converting regular and digital films to the Imax format.

Imax reported net earnings of C$4.9 million or C$0.32 a share on revenues of C$37.7 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, compared to net earnings of C$1.3 million or C$0.08 on revenues of C$29.5 million in 1995.
